# Lines stripped from MARLEY output before the golden-file comparison.
#
# ONE source of truth. These expressions were previously written out by hand
# at three places in ci.yml, and -- worse -- were not part of the cache key
# for the golden file. Editing them therefore produced a current file
# filtered one way and a cached golden file filtered another: a guaranteed
# failure, and the reason such a change previously had to land by itself.
# The cache key now includes a hash of this file, so editing it invalidates
# the golden file automatically and precisely.
#
# MUST be used as:
#
#   grep -v -f <(grep -v -e '^#' -e '^$' .github/golden-filters.txt) FILE
#
# Comments and blank lines have to be stripped first, and the blank-line
# part is not cosmetic: grep -f treats an EMPTY pattern as matching every
# line. Passing this file to grep -f directly would filter the golden file
# and the current file both down to nothing, and diff would then pass --
# silently retiring the entire physics comparison while looking green.
#
# Each surviving line is a basic regular expression.

# Run timestamp.
^T MARLEY

# HepMC3 library version, which tracks the build environment.
^HepMC::Version

# The serialised PARSED job configuration, not a copy of the file. It is
# produced by whichever MARLEY version ran, so any difference in how two
# versions parse, normalise, default or NAME a configuration key lands here
# -- and the golden file comes from the reference branch while the current
# file comes from the branch under test. None of that is a physics
# regression.
#
# Not hypothetical: an older output in this tree records the generate block
# as "executable_settings" where a newer one records "generate". Had that
# rename arrived in a pull request, the golden diff would have gone red for
# byte-identical physics.
#
# The cost, stated rather than glossed: a genuine unintended change to the
# stored configuration will no longer be caught here. That is acceptable
# because this diff exists to catch physics regressions, and the
# configuration schema has its own consumers -- "resume" and "reweight" --
# that would notice.
^A MARLEY.JSONconfig
